gaps.explanation: Users view WordPress as a platform to run an income-generating business rather than a simple personal journaling app. When mobile-only creators cannot manage monetization plugins or discover earning mechanisms, they feel abandoned at a key stage of site growth. Addressing this requires exposing mobile-friendly plugin/monetization workflows instead of forcing desktop fallbacks.

gaps.userNeed: I need explicit control over when my changes are saved and an unambiguous way to undo edits so I can experiment with content formatting without fear of permanently ruining my draft.
gaps.explanation: Authors experience significant friction and anxiety when continuous background auto-saving modifies live drafts without granular undo points on mobile touch keyboards. The product treats auto-saving as a convenience, whereas authors require clear non-destructive editing boundaries to feel safe composing complex posts on mobile. Providing explicit revision history and reliable undo/redo capabilities directly resolves this psychological safety gap.
gaps.confidenceJustification: 88% — corroborated by explicit user feedback regarding auto-save anxiety and closed issue #21189 which addressed visual confirmation of UNDO but missed the underlying need for explicit state control.
gaps.verdictReason: GitHub issue #21189 addressed visual confirmation feedback for site restoration, but failed to solve the writer's need for granular undo history and manual draft state control during live text editing.

gaps.userNeed: I need complete parity with desktop site structure tools like categories and templates so I can publish fully-organized content directly from my mobile device.
gaps.explanation: Mobile-first creators rely on the app to maintain their site's structure on the go, but missing category trees or template options breaks their publishing pipeline. When category structures fail to sync, users are forced to delay publishing or switch to desktop browsers, defeating the purpose of a mobile content management app. Full structural taxonomy parity ensures creators can reliably execute complete publishing workflows natively on Android.

gaps.counterArgument: The cited evidence reflects transient sync bugs and niche power-user edge cases rather than a broad, unaddressed latent need for full desktop taxonomy parity.
